messages:
brightport_ops: Hey team — starting ~09:12 UTC we started getting 403s from Redwood API for our Private deployment. Our security team says we didn't change the allowlist. previous egress was 52.14.23.101, now requests are coming from 52.14.24.178. Any idea if you rotated NAT/EIP or something?

jess_support: Sorry about the disruption — can you paste the curl you used and the raw response body? Also which region and VPC id?

brightport_ops: curl -v "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{\"prompt\":\"hi\"}'
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (52.14.24.178) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Authorization: Bearer <key>
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< content-type: application/json
< {"error":"Forbidden: request origin not allowlisted"}

We are in us-east-1, VPC vpc-0a1b2c3d, using a NAT gateway with an attached EIP. We haven't changed infra in days.

alex_oncall: Quick check: if your NAT was replaced (eg via autoscaling or an infra change), EIP can move. Do you see any CloudTrail events for Elastic IP disassociation?

mike_infra: Also check the route table for the private subnet — if the subnet got switched to a different NAT or a new AZ was spun up with a different EIP, outbound IP will change. Could be Terraform reconciliation.

brightport_ops: CloudTrail shows ElasticIpAssociation for nat-089c... at 09:10 UTC, looks like a new association. Not sure what triggered it.

jess_support: Thanks — that explains it. On our side we log the source IPs we see on incoming connections. infra-bot generated this at 09:13:

infra-bot: Event: egress-ip-change detected for tenant brightport-corp. Previous: 52.14.23.101 New: 52.14.24.178 TTL: 5m (automated detection)

jess_support: We can whitelist the new /32 IPs temporarily, but recommend either: 1) add both the old and new EIPs to your allowlist, or 2) whitelist our published CIDR block (if your security policy allows), or 3) set up a stable egress using Elastic IP + static NAT (cloud side) or request our Static Egress Add-on (we can reserve an outbound IP for your Private deployment).

emma_engineer: If you want a quick workaround, update the allowlist to include 52.14.24.178/32 and retry. For longer term, consider using DNS-based allowlist with TLS client certs or mutual-TLS.

brightport_ops: We updated the allowlist to include 52.14.24.178 and retried — requests succeeded. Thanks.

jess_support: Glad that's working. A couple of follow-ups: can you confirm why the NAT replaced? If Terraform applied or if you have a health-check that recreates the NAT it can cause EIP to move. If you want, we can check our logs for the exact handshake and time window for the incident.

brightport_ops: Looks like our autoscaling stack replaced the NAT gateway when we pushed a minor subnet change via Terraform. We misconfigured the lifecycle rules so EIP wasn't preserved. We'll fix that.

mike_infra: Common Terraform pattern: attach EIP resource and set create_before_destroy on NAT gateway or manage EIP association separately. Otherwise a destroy/create cycle will reassign IPs. Also check provider policies for EIP reuse (some clouds don't guarantee same numeric).

jess_support: I created a short KB for customers facing this: `https://docs.redwood.ai/private/egress-ip-rotation` with recommended infra patterns and contact points for our Static Egress Add-on. I'll paste key items here:
- Always treat EIP association as mutable unless you explicitly reserve with `allocation_id` and avoid replacing the NAT gateway resource.
- Use `create_before_destroy` or keep EIP as a separate resource.
- Consider using our Static Egress Add-on to get a stable outbound IP pool.
- For immediate recovery: add new IP /32 to allowlist or widen to CIDR block for the region.

brightport_ops: Appreciate the KB. One last question — do you have any tooling to alert us if our outbound IP changes from what we expected?

infra-bot: Tip: enable egress-ip-monitoring in Console -> Networking -> Alerts. It will notify both your ops and support if external egress IPs change.

brightport_ops: Turned it on. We'll also update our Terraform. Thanks for the quick help, resolved on our side. :thumbsup:

jess_support: Marking this thread resolved. If you want us to reserve static egress IPs for you, open a ticket with account id and region and we'll scope it.
